metadata.title: COSU Clean-Room / Facility Access Terminal SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan defining Corporate-Owned Single-Use (COSU) Clean-Room and Facility Access Terminals as constrained, access-enforcement endpoint execution environments.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional security and privacy baseline profile.

system-characteristics.system-description: A corporate-owned, single-use endpoint dedicated to verifying authorization, enforcing access conditions, and logging entry into controlled environments such as clean rooms, secure labs, and regulated facilities.

props.name: inherits-from-sspp
props.remarks: COSU Clean-Room and Facility Access Terminals inherit foundational endpoint trust governance from the Secure Endpoint Platform SSPP.

props.name: endpoint-class
props.remarks: Single-use COSU endpoint for physical access enforcement and environmental entry control.

props.name: execution-model
props.remarks: Execution is restricted to approved access control, identity verification, badge, biometric, and environmental compliance applications.

props.name: user-authentication-model
props.remarks: Users authenticate for access verification (e.g., badge, biometric, PIN, or federated identity) without persistent local sessions.

props.name: ownership-model
props.remarks: Clean-Room and Facility Access Terminals are owned by the institution.

props.name: management-model
props.remarks: Access Terminals are centrally enrolled, configured, monitored, and recovered.

props.name: cryptographic-identity
props.remarks: Device identity is used to establish trust with access control systems, logging services, and management platforms.

props.name: baseline-hardening
props.remarks: Operating system configuration disables shell access, general applications, removable media, and unauthorized interfaces.

props.name: environmental-compliance-checks
props.remarks: Where required, terminals enforce entry conditions such as training status, certification validity, gowning acknowledgements, or safety confirmations.

props.name: network-access-model
props.remarks: Network access is restricted to physical access control systems, identity verification services, logging platforms, and management endpoints.

props.name: data-persistence
props.remarks: Local persistence is limited to encrypted, transient access events or logs required for continuity and troubleshooting.

props.name: eligible-data-classifications
props.remarks: Access Terminals may process limited operational and identity metadata but no research, administrative, or regulated datasets.

props.name: non-equivalence-statement
props.remarks: Authorization to enter controlled spaces does not imply eligibility for system administration, data access, or elevated endpoint trust tiers.

props.name: availability-requirement
props.remarks: Access Terminals must prioritize uptime and rapid recovery to avoid disrupting facility operations.

props.name: monitoring-and-integrity-signals
props.remarks: Terminal health, authentication attempts, access decisions, and tamper events are continuously monitored.

props.name: lifecycle-governance
props.remarks: Provisioning, maintenance, reset, and retirement of Access Terminals are auditable and subject to change control.

system-implementation.remarks: COSU Clean-Room and Facility Access Terminals implement Secure Endpoint patterns with emphasis on access integrity, auditability, and operational continuity.

roles.title: Facility Access Operations
roles.remarks: Responsible for daily operation, monitoring, and response involving Access Terminals.

roles.title: Facility Governance Authority
roles.remarks: Approves access conditions, identity requirements, and compliance dependencies for controlled environments.

roles.title: Endpoint Security Operations
roles.remarks: Ensures security posture, monitoring, and lifecycle governance for Access Terminals.

control-implementation.remarks: Clean-Room and Facility Access Terminal implementations may use hardened workstations, industrial touch panels, or embedded controllers and are maintained as tightly controlled configuration baselines.
